video_caption: The video opens at 0:00 with a man wearing a black cap with a white Puma logo and a blue, white, and grey striped t-shirt, sitting at a wooden desk and speaking directly to the camera. He actively uses hand gestures, including open palms, pointing fingers, and shrugging, to emphasize his points. In front of him is a black microphone on a small tripod, a wooden tablet stand holding a smartphone to his left, and a silver laptop to his right. A film clapboard with "BENSGUIDE STUDIOS" text is visible on the far left. The background features white walls, shelves with decorative string lights, and a black monitor. At 0:13, the scene transitions to a bright blue background where a light blue film reel rotates into view on the right, as black text "FILMAKING" appears on the left, followed by "CONTENT CREATION" and "Tutorials" below it. A quick montage from 0:15 to 0:22 shows various video production and photography-related clips. The first clip (0:15-0:18) is an on-set shooting scenario in a large, empty industrial space, featuring several individuals including one holding a boom mic, another gesturing, a woman using a laptop, and a man in a cap talking to a woman, with a film camera on a tripod visible. Overlaid text on the right reads "ON SET shooting capturing video." This transitions (0:18-0:21) to four film strip-like frames: the top left shows a silhouette of a person photographing a sunset with the text "LANDSCAPES"; the top right shows a person photographing a woman, labeled "PORTRAITS"; the bottom left displays fire/flames with "BROLL" text; and the bottom right features a neon sign of a film clapboard with "time for VIDEO" (English) and the text "CONTENT CREATION." At 0:21, a black silhouette of a film camera projects a light beam onto a blue background, revealing "BENSGUIDE" (in yellow brushstroke font) and "PHOTO & VIDEO" (in black distressed font) within the beam. The man returns to the desk scene at 0:23, continuing to talk and gesture with open palms, before a screen recording at 0:28 shows a YouTube search for "How to post on instagram from computer" and its various auto-completion suggestions like "how to post on instagram from computer mac" and "how to post on instagram on pc." At 0:34, the search results page is displayed, showcasing multiple YouTube videos on the topic, many by "Bensguide." The man reappears at 0:42, expressing frustration with Instagram's lack of a direct PC posting feature, picking up his smartphone with a blue cover, and then gesturing animatedly as he promises to demonstrate a free and easy method.

In a split-screen video from 0:04 to 0:07, a man wearing a black cap and a striped t-shirt is speaking to the camera, gesturing with his left hand. He is seated at a desk with a microphone in front of him and a laptop to his right, against a background of shelves with potted plants and other items. The left side of the screen displays a smartphone's home screen, showing various app icons, including Gmail, Samsung, WhatsApp, and Instagram. The phone's background is a photo of a child sitting by a body of water, with the date "Mon, 28 January" and time "14:53" visible, along with weather details "10° Edinburgh." A "DU RECORDER" label is present at the bottom of the smartphone screen.

From 00:03 to 00:15, a light-skinned man with short dark hair and a beard, wearing a black baseball cap with a white Puma logo and a blue and white striped t-shirt, sits at a wooden desk, looking directly at the camera. He has tattoos on his left forearm. He is speaking into a black microphone on a small tripod positioned in front of him, using expressive hand gestures. Behind him, a white shelving unit is adorned with string lights, plants, and various items, while a black monitor is visible on a desk to his right. Starting around 00:09, animated overlay graphics appear at the bottom of the screen: a thumbs-up icon with the text "LIKE THE VIDEO", a red bell icon with the text "SUBSCRIBE", and another bell icon with the text "GET NOTIFIED", all designed to encourage viewer interaction.

The video opens with a clean white Google search page. A mouse cursor types "instagram creator studio" into the search bar, which is highlighted with a blue box containing the text "TYPE IN INSTAGRAM CREATOR STUDIO." The search results page loads, and the cursor clicks on a link titled "Facebook Creator Studio," which leads to the business.facebook.com domain. A chart on the right displays trend data for "instagram creator studio." The screen then transitions to a loading page before displaying the Facebook Creator Studio interface. A purple bar at the top indicates it's the Creator Studio, initially showing a dropdown with account names ("benguides," "Claddtech," "PSTutorials"). The main content area shows "Monetisation" and "Brand Collabs Manager," along with a blue pop-up stating, "See scheduled and published posts with the calendar view." The cursor then clicks on the Instagram icon in the purple bar, switching the view. The screen briefly shows a "Home" page with "Recent posts" and "Insights," and a small pop-up reading, "Instagram has a new calendar tool. Click here to try it out." Finally, it transitions to "Content library > Posts," displaying a list of Instagram posts with details like "Post status," "Date," "Likes," and "Comments."

The video demonstrates the navigation and functionality of the Instagram Creator Studio interface within a web browser. It begins on the "Content library - Posts" page, where a list of past Instagram posts is displayed with details like status, date, likes, and comments, and a date range filter showing "1 Jan 2009 - 28 Jan 2021". On the left sidebar, the user clicks through various options: first "Calendar" to show a monthly calendar view for "January 2021", then "Insights", revealing sub-sections. "Activity" shows "0 Posts" and "Interactions" with a line graph of "Actions taken on your account" from "21 Jan 2021 - 27 Jan 2021". Subsequently, "Audience" is selected, displaying "1.2K Total followers" and a bar chart of "Age and gender of your followers" showing "56% Men" and "44% Women". The user then hovers over "Monetisation", which has a dropdown arrow, and clicks on "Instagram accounts", revealing a page with the Instagram account "Ben Taylor | Photographer bensguides" and "1,188" followers, along with an "Add Instagram Account" button. Next, "Resources" is clicked, opening a dropdown menu with options like "Ads Manager", "Events", "Instant Articles", and "Shop". Finally, the user clicks the "Create Post" button at the top left, which opens a dropdown with "Instagram feed" and "IGTV" options. As the "Instagram feed" option is discussed, the screen visually transitions: the previous content slides away, and a new "Post to Instagram feed" window appears on the right, providing fields to "Write your caption...", "Add location", and "Add content", along with "Post info" and "Advanced settings" sections, and a "Publish" button.

At the 0:02 mark, a computer screen displays a web browser on "business.facebook.com/creatorstudio/tab/instagram_accounts". On the left, a dark blue sidebar shows navigation options, with "Instagram accounts" highlighted, and a profile card for "Ben Taylor | Photographer". The main content area features a large white pop-up window titled "Post to Instagram feed" (meaning: the purpose of this window is to create a post for an Instagram feed). This pop-up includes sections for "Your post" with a "Write your caption..." text box, a character/hashtag counter ("Remaining: 2200 characters 30 hashtags"), and an "Add location" field. Below this, a grey box with a camera icon and text "Add content" and "+ Add content" prompts the user to "Choose the photos or videos that you'd like to post". On the right side of the pop-up, a smaller sidebar shows "Post info" (highlighted) with the description "Add the information needed to create your post," and "Advanced settings" with its description "Advanced settings for comments, branded content and more." A blue "Publish" button is visible at the bottom right of the pop-up.

The video segment displays a screen recording of a web browser, specifically the Facebook Creator Studio interface for Instagram accounts. The left sidebar shows navigation options, with "Instagram accounts" currently selected and highlighted. The main content area displays "Instagram accounts" with a profile labeled "Ben Taylor | Photographer" and username "bentaylorpics". A pop-up window overlays the screen, titled "Post to Instagram feed". Inside this pop-up, a video preview shows a person standing in a snowy forest. A blue banner above the video reads "New! You can now choose a custom thumbnail from any of your video's frames." Below the video, there's a section to "Post to Facebook" with a checkbox next to "Psn tutorials" and a blue banner stating "New! Tag people in your videos." On the right side of the pop-up, under "Post info," the text "Add the information needed to create your post" is visible, followed by "Cover image" with a small thumbnail (matching the video) and the text "Select cover thumbnail for your video." Further down are "Advanced settings" for comments and branded content. At the very bottom, a green progress bar shows "100%", alongside a blue "Publish" button and a partially visible "Save as Draft" button. A mouse cursor is seen moving over the "Post info" section and then briefly over "Cover image".

A man wearing a black baseball cap with a white Puma logo, a striped t-shirt (white, blue, and black stripes), and a watch on his left wrist, sits at a wooden desk, speaking directly to the camera with an open mouth and wide eyes, gesturing with both hands. In front of him is a black microphone on a small tripod. To his left, there's a wooden stand holding a tablet or phone, and behind it, a black and white film clapperboard is visible, with text that reads "FILM/MEDIA STUDIOS TAKE ROLL DIRECTOR C. BALAMAN". To his right, a black laptop is open. The background features a white wall with white shelves adorned with string lights, a green plant, and a black monitor on a desk to the right.
